# Vibe

> A fast, minimal player for your music files on Mac, iPhone and iPad. Plays audio files you
> own — on disk, or in a file provider such as iCloud Drive or Dropbox — with
> a seekable full-track waveform and DJ performance FX. There is no catalogue,
> library to import, Vibe account or subscription. The Mac also has a
> turntable-style pitch fader.

Vibe is a native macOS and iOS app written in Objective-C on its own CoreAudio playback
engine, with no third-party audio engine. It is free, open source under
Apache 2.0, and available on the App Store. macOS also has a direct download.

- Requires macOS 13 Ventura or later (Apple silicon or Intel), or iOS 26 or later.
- Formats: MP3, MP2, AAC/ADTS, FLAC, MP4/M4A/M4B/M4R, CAF, W64, Ogg Opus and
  Vorbis, QTA (Voice Memos), AIFF, WAV, and CUE sheets — all played by Vibe's
  own engine. QTA requires macOS. Audio is decoded to float32.
- No library or database: drop a file or folder on the window and it plays.
  Tags, artwork and BPM are read in the background and cached to disk.
- Files may live anywhere the Files system can reach — a local disk, an
  external drive, iCloud Drive, Dropbox or another file provider. Vibe asks
  the operating system to fetch a cloud file and shows its download progress;
  iOS also has a direct Dropbox connection.
- Both platforms have BPM detection and DJ FX: low-kill, reverb and delays
  locked to the track's BPM. The Mac adds a pitch fader, key analysis,
  keyboard FX controls and skips measured in bars when the tempo is known.
- Localized into 30 languages.
- Open URL… plays an audio file from a web address. Plain http is allowed
  only to the local network. The download is kept for replay.
- Collects no personal information. Vibe goes online only to fetch an address
  the user types into Open URL…, on iPhone and iPad to reach Dropbox if
  connected, and in the Mac version downloaded from vibeplayer.app to check
  for and download updates. Each update check names the app version, the
  macOS version, the architecture, the beta setting, and the app's language.
  It also says whether it is that copy's first check of the day, the week, or
  the month. The site counts these without recording anything that
  identifies the user. Vibe has no account and no servers beyond the
  website. On the Mac the outgoing network entitlement is used only for
  those requests.
  Cloud files are fetched by the provider's own system extension, not by Vibe.

## Links

- [Home](https://vibeplayer.app/): what the app is, with screenshots.
- [Privacy policy](https://vibeplayer.app/privacy): what Vibe stores locally,
  and its network requests.
- [Download (.dmg)](https://vibeplayer.app/download/latest): always the
  current notarized universal disk image — a redirect to the release asset on
  GitHub, where an arm64-only alternate is also available.
- [Homebrew](https://github.com/cmicali/homebrew-tap): `brew install
  cmicali/tap/vibe` installs the same notarized disk image, and `brew upgrade`
  follows each stable release.
- [Release notes](https://github.com/cmicali/vibe/releases): every version,
  with what changed in each.
- [Mac App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/vibe-music-player/id1582482361?mt=12)
- [Source code](https://github.com/cmicali/vibe): Apache 2.0.
- [Support](https://vibeplayer.app/support): the GitHub issue tracker.
